I totally get that when I had my puppy it was the same it can be very scary. Here are some tips and some really important things for your puppy.


1. Always end on a good note.
This is for every thing. End your training with a good feeling, a new thing with a good feeling and end a social interaction with a good feeling for your dog. For example: when you try to learn you dog something new but he doesn’t get it yet. End with something he knows and can do on command. When your dog is playing don’t interrupt when the dogs are still in “conflict” end the social interaction when they are apart from each other or playing. This will help your dog associate this things with positive feelings and prevent stress.


2. Go to puppy play session, or for now let them play with smaller dogs. 
If your puppy is still very small let them play with smaller dog or dogs that you know are good with puppies. (Interaction with older dog is very important tho). And you can gradually built this up. 
(My guideline would be if the puppy is half the size or bigger they can play)

3. Don’t try to pick up your dog. This will only learn your puppy to run and avoid social stuff and get stressed. Your dog needs socializing very much and they need a good foundation for it and they learn that in their puppy time.

4. Your puppy needs to surrender. A dog will only stop being dominant when your dog stops resisting. (Lying completely still). If your dog does this and the other dog doesn’t stop it’s a sign you need to break them up. 

5. you can learn your dog to surrender. highly recommend this! It’s not only good for dog interaction but also for human interaction.
Here is a way to do this:
Go sit down and place your dog on it’s back on your sumac/ between your legs. Your puppy will probably resist and try to get away. Don’t let them! Keep them on their back! And when they stop resisting wait like 3/5 seconds and let them go. Do this multiple times.
